officialTitle: AI Factory doesn't eliminate the fundamentals

chapters.title: Introduction: AI adoption across the SDLC
Why a fast prototype still takes time to reach production
Three different meanings of using AI
The AI factory: six stations and six fundamentals
Making enterprise architecture readable to agents
Assessment findings and risk moving downstream
Following one change through the factory
Making controls and audit evidence executable
Autonomy levels, prototypes and changing roles
Where to start and where to reinvest the time saved

existingSummary: Sini Tistelgrén argues that an AI factory depends on clear intent, sound architecture, security, independent verification, ownership and operational feedback. She follows a change through six delivery stages and explains how enterprises can turn existing controls into executable checks while reshaping roles and measuring outcomes.
